name: Alexander von Humboldt
summary: German naturalist and explorer who, with Carl Ritter, founded modern geography and studied nature as an interconnected whole through fieldwork in the Americas.

name: Friedrich Ratzel
summary: German geographer who founded anthropogeography and modern political geography and is regarded as a founder of environmental determinism.

name: Ellen Churchill Semple
summary: American geographer and student of Ratzel who spread environmental determinism in the English-speaking world.

name: Ellsworth Huntington
summary: American geographer who argued that climate shapes human energy and the rise and fall of civilisations.

name: Paul Vidal de la Blache
summary: French geographer and founder of the French school of human geography, whose regional studies of pays and genre de vie underlie possibilism.

name: Lucien Febvre
summary: French historian of the Annales school who coined the term possibilism for the ideas of Vidal de la Blache.

name: Griffith Taylor
summary: British-born Australian geographer who proposed neo-determinism as a middle path between determinism and possibilism.

name: Alfred Hettner
summary: German geographer who defined geography as a chorological science of the differing character of areas and regions.

name: Richard Hartshorne
summary: American geographer who defined geography as the study of areal differentiation and defended its regional and idiographic character.
note: Husain's main text gives 1899-1992; his biographic notes print 1935-1992.

name: Fred K. Schaefer
summary: German-born American geographer who attacked Hartshorne's exceptionalism and called for geography as a law-seeking spatial science.

name: Carl O. Sauer
summary: American geographer of the Berkeley school who studied the cultural landscape and the human transformation of nature.

name: David Harvey
summary: British geographer who moved from positivist method in Explanation in Geography to Marxist and radical geography.

name: Yi-Fu Tuan
summary: Chinese-born American geographer and leading figure of humanistic geography who wrote on space, place and the human bond with place.

name: Torsten Hägerstrand
summary: Swedish geographer who modelled the spatial diffusion of innovations and founded time geography.

name: Halford Mackinder
summary: British geographer and politician whose Heartland theory held that control of the interior of Eurasia is the key to world power.

name: Nicholas J. Spykman
summary: Dutch-American political scientist who argued that the Rimland around Eurasia, not the Heartland, is the key to world power.

name: Walter Christaller
summary: German geographer who developed central place theory from a study of settlements in southern Germany.

name: August Lösch
summary: German economist who extended central place ideas into a general theory of economic landscapes built of hexagonal market areas.

name: Johann Heinrich von Thünen
summary: German landowner and economist who modelled concentric rings of agricultural land use around a single central market.

name: Alfred Weber
summary: German economist and sociologist who developed the least-cost theory of industrial location.
note: Brother of the sociologist Max Weber; not to be confused with him.

name: W.W. Rostow
summary: American economic historian who proposed five stages of economic growth from traditional society to the age of high mass consumption.

name: Gunnar Myrdal
summary: Swedish economist who argued that market forces widen regional inequality through cumulative causation and backwash effects.

name: François Perroux
summary: French economist who proposed growth poles of propulsive industries in abstract economic space.

name: Albert O. Hirschman
summary: German-born American economist who advocated unbalanced growth and described trickling-down and polarisation effects between regions.

name: John Friedmann
summary: Austrian-born American planner who proposed the core-periphery model of regional development.

name: Wilbur Zelinsky
summary: American geographer who proposed the hypothesis of the mobility transition linking types of migration to stages of modernisation.

name: Thomas Robert Malthus
summary: English clergyman and economist who argued that population tends to grow faster than the means of subsistence.
note: Majid Husain prints 1760-1834 in both the text and the biographic notes.

name: Frank W. Notestein
summary: American demographer who formulated the classic theory of demographic transition.

name: E.G. Ravenstein
summary: German-born British geographer who stated laws of migration from British census data.

name: Everett S. Lee
summary: American demographer who explained migration through factors at origin and destination, intervening obstacles and personal factors.

name: Ester Boserup
summary: Danish economist who argued against Malthus that population growth drives agricultural intensification.

name: Mark Jefferson
summary: American geographer who described the primate city as a leading city disproportionately larger than the others.

name: George Kingsley Zipf
summary: American linguist who popularised the rank-size rule for the sizes of cities.

name: Ernest W. Burgess
summary: American sociologist of the Chicago school who proposed the concentric zone model of urban structure.

name: Homer Hoyt
summary: American land economist who proposed the sector model of urban residential land use.

name: Chauncy D. Harris
summary: American geographer who with Edward Ullman proposed the multiple nuclei model of urban land use.

name: Patrick Geddes
summary: Scottish biologist and town planner who coined the term conurbation and pioneered regional survey as the basis of planning.

name: Jean Gottmann
summary: French geographer who used the term megalopolis for the urbanised northeastern seaboard of the United States.

name: William Morris Davis
summary: American geographer and geomorphologist who proposed the cycle of erosion in which landscapes pass through youth, maturity and old age.

name: Walther Penck
summary: German geomorphologist who related landform development to the rate of uplift against the rate of denudation.
note: Son of the glacial geomorphologist Albrecht Penck.

name: Lester C. King
summary: South African geomorphologist who proposed pediplanation through the parallel retreat of slopes.

name: James Hutton
summary: Scottish geologist, often called the father of modern geology, who stated the principle of uniformitarianism.

name: Alfred Wegener
summary: German meteorologist who proposed the theory of continental drift.

name: Harry H. Hess
summary: American geologist who proposed sea-floor spreading from the mid-ocean ridges.

name: Arthur Holmes
summary: British geologist who proposed convection currents in the mantle as the force that moves the continents.

name: Clarence Dutton
summary: American geologist who coined the term isostasy.
note: Husain gives 1841-1912; Savindra Singh gives 1843-1912.

name: Wladimir Köppen
summary: German-Russian climatologist who devised the most widely used empirical classification of climates.

name: C.W. Thornthwaite
summary: American climatologist who classified climates by precipitation effectiveness and later by potential evapotranspiration.

name: Charles Darwin
summary: English naturalist who, besides his theory of evolution, proposed the subsidence theory of coral reefs.

name: Arthur Tansley
summary: British ecologist who coined the term ecosystem.

name: Derwent Whittlesey
summary: American geographer who divided the world into major agricultural regions and introduced the idea of sequent occupance.

name: Anthropogeographie
summary: Two-volume foundation of human geography that studies how the physical environment influences human societies.
note: Volume 1 appeared in 1882 and volume 2 in 1891.

name: Influences of Geographic Environment
aliases: Influences of Geographic Environment on the Basis of Ratzel's System of Anthropo-Geography
summary: Restates Ratzel's anthropogeography for English readers and opens with the claim that man is a product of the earth's surface.

name: Civilization and Climate
summary: Argues that civilisation flourishes in stimulating climates and links human energy and progress to climate and weather.

name: Principles of Human Geography
aliases: Principes de géographie humaine|Principes de geographie humaine
summary: Sets out human geography as the study of genres de vie and the relations between people and their milieu.
note: Published after his death and edited by de Martonne; English translation 1926.

name: The Nature of Geography
summary: Surveys geographic thought and defines geography as the study of areal differentiation of the earth's surface.

name: Exceptionalism in Geography: A Methodological Examination
summary: Paper attacking Hartshorne's view of geography as an exceptional discipline and calling for a spatial science that seeks laws.
note: Published after Schaefer's death in 1953.

name: The Geographical Pivot of History
summary: Paper read to the Royal Geographical Society naming the pivot area of Eurasia as the seat of world power in the post-Columbian age.

name: Democratic Ideals and Reality
summary: Renames the pivot area the Heartland and states the dictum linking East Europe, the Heartland and the World-Island.

name: The Geography of the Peace
summary: Posthumous book setting out the Rimland theory as a counter to Mackinder's Heartland.

name: Central Places in Southern Germany
aliases: Die zentralen Orte in Süddeutschland|Central Places
summary: Study of the towns of southern Germany that sets out central place theory.
note: German original 1933; English translation 1966.

name: The Economics of Location
aliases: Die räumliche Ordnung der Wirtschaft|Economics of Location
summary: Builds a general theory of location in which hexagonal market areas of many goods form an economic landscape.
note: German original 1940; English translation 1954.

name: The Isolated State
aliases: Der isolierte Staat|Isolated State|von Thünen model|Von Thunen model
summary: Models agricultural land use as concentric rings around a central city, set by economic rent and the cost of transport to market.

name: Theory of the Location of Industries
aliases: Über den Standort der Industrien|Location of Industries
summary: Sets out the least-cost theory of industrial location.
note: German original 1909; English translation by C.J. Friedrich 1929.

name: The Stages of Economic Growth
aliases: Stages of Economic Growth|Rostow's model|Rostow model|stages of growth model
summary: Proposes five stages: traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity and the age of high mass consumption.
note: Subtitled A Non-Communist Manifesto.

name: Economic Theory and Under-developed Regions
summary: Sets out circular and cumulative causation and the backwash and spread effects between rich and poor regions.

name: An Essay on the Principle of Population
aliases: Essay on the Principle of Population|Malthusian theory|Malthusian theory of population
summary: Argues that population grows geometrically and food arithmetically, so positive and preventive checks hold population to subsistence.

name: A Theory of Migration
aliases: Lee's theory of migration|Lee's model of migration|push-pull model
summary: Explains migration by factors at origin and destination, intervening obstacles and personal factors.

name: The Laws of Migration
summary: States laws of migration such as most migrants moving short distances, by stages, towards great centres of commerce, each stream producing a counter-stream.
note: Two papers: 1885 and 1889.

name: The Conditions of Agricultural Growth
summary: Argues against Malthus that population pressure leads farmers to intensify land use and adopt new techniques.

name: The Origin of Continents and Oceans
aliases: Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane|Origin of Continents and Oceans
summary: Sets out continental drift with evidence from matching coastlines, fossils, rocks and past climates.
note: Revised in several later editions.

name: Morphological Analysis of Land Forms
aliases: Die morphologische Analyse|Morphological Analysis of Landforms
summary: Relates the form of landscapes and slopes to the rates of crustal uplift and denudation.
note: German original 1924 published after his death; English translation 1953.

name: Explanation in Geography
summary: Sets out the philosophy and methods of positivist scientific geography during the quantitative revolution.

name: Social Justice and the City
summary: Marks Harvey's turn from liberal to Marxist analysis of urban inequality and is a founding text of radical geography.

name: Topophilia
aliases: Topophilia: A Study of Environmental Perception
summary: Studies the affective bond between people and place and is a founding text of humanistic geography.
note: Husain's glossary says Tuan introduced the term to geography in 1961.

name: Environmental determinism
summary: The view that the physical environment, especially climate and terrain, controls human activities and the course of history.
note: Ratzel, Semple and Huntington are its main exponents.

name: Lebensraum
aliases: living space|organic theory of the state
summary: Ratzel's idea that the state, like an organism, needs living space and grows by expanding its territory.
note: Later used by German geopolitics under Haushofer.

name: Possibilism
summary: The view that nature offers possibilities and people choose among them, so human choice, not the environment, decides ways of life.
note: Husain: advocated by Vidal de la Blache's school; Febvre postulated the term.

name: Genre de vie
summary: Vidal's term for the way of life of a group, shaped by the physical, historical and social influences of its region.
note: Husain makes it central to Vidal de la Blache's work; one passage says Febvre coined the term.

name: Neo-determinism
summary: Taylor's view that people can speed, slow or stop a region's development but cannot change the course that nature sets.

name: Chorology
summary: The view of geography as the study of the varying character of the earth's surface, area by area.

name: Areal differentiation
summary: Hartshorne's definition of geography as the description and interpretation of the variable character of the earth's surface from place to place.
note: Set out in The Nature of Geography (1939).

name: Quantitative revolution
summary: The shift in geography in the 1950s and 1960s to statistical methods, models and the search for spatial laws.

name: Radical geography
summary: A Marxist-influenced approach from the late 1960s that studies poverty, inequality and injustice as products of capitalist space.

name: Humanistic geography
summary: An approach that studies human experience, perception and the meaning of place, against positivist spatial science.

name: Cultural landscape
summary: Sauer's idea that a cultural group, working on the natural landscape over time, produces a cultural landscape.

name: Spatial diffusion of innovations
summary: Hägerstrand's model of how innovations spread across space through personal contact, with adoption falling off with distance.
note: Swedish original 1953; English translation 1967.

name: Heartland
summary: Mackinder's idea that the interior of Eurasia, safe from sea power, is the pivot of world power.
note: Called the Pivot Area in 1904; renamed the Heartland in Democratic Ideals and Reality (1919), with the dictum on East Europe and the World-Island.

name: Rimland
summary: Spykman's idea that the coastal fringe around Eurasia holds the key to world power: who controls the Rimland rules Eurasia.
note: Set out in The Geography of the Peace (1944).

name: Central place theory
aliases: central place|central place model|Christaller's model|hierarchy of central places
summary: Settlements serving their surrounding areas form a hierarchy of hexagonal market areas arranged by marketing (K=3), transport (K=4) or administrative (K=7) principles.
note: German original 1933; English translation 1966.

name: Least-cost theory of industrial location
aliases: Weber's theory of industrial location|Weber's model|least cost location theory|isodapane|locational triangle|material index
summary: Industry locates where total transport and labour costs are least, found with the locational triangle, the material index and isodapanes.
note: German original 1909; English translation 1929.

name: Cumulative causation
aliases: circular and cumulative causation|cumulative causation theory|backwash effects|spread effects|backwash and spread effects
summary: Myrdal's idea that a region's initial advantage is built on by market forces, so backwash effects outweigh spread effects and regional inequality widens.

name: Growth pole
aliases: growth pole theory|pôle de croissance|growth centre|growth center
summary: Perroux's idea that growth starts at poles of propulsive industries and spreads unevenly through the economy.
note: Some books date it to his 1950 paper on economic space; Boudeville gave it a regional meaning as growth centres.

name: Core-periphery model
summary: Friedmann's model in which a dominant core region grows at the expense of a dependent periphery through stages of spatial development.
note: Set out in Regional Development Policy: A Case Study of Venezuela (1966).

name: Trickling-down and polarisation effects
aliases: trickle-down effect|trickling-down effect|polarisation effect|polarization effect|unbalanced growth
summary: Hirschman's terms for growth spreading from developed to lagging regions (trickling down) and growth concentrating in the core (polarisation).
note: Set out in The Strategy of Economic Development (1958).

name: Demographic transition
summary: The model in which a population moves from high birth and death rates, through falling death rates, to low birth and death rates.
note: First outlined by Warren Thompson in 1929; Notestein's 1945 version is the classic statement.

name: Mobility transition
aliases: hypothesis of the mobility transition|Zelinsky model|Zelinsky's model
summary: Zelinsky's hypothesis that patterns of migration change in step with the stages of the demographic transition and modernisation.

name: Primate city
aliases: law of the primate city|primacy|urban primacy
summary: A country's leading city that is disproportionately larger than the next cities and expresses national life and feeling.

name: Rank-size rule
summary: The population of the city of rank n equals the population of the largest city divided by n.
note: First noted by Felix Auerbach in 1913; Zipf popularised it in 1949.

name: Concentric zone model
summary: Burgess's model of a city growing outward in five concentric zones around the central business district.

name: Sector model
summary: Hoyt's model in which residential areas grow outward in wedge-shaped sectors along transport routes from the centre.

name: Multiple nuclei model
aliases: multiple nuclei theory|Harris and Ullman model
summary: Harris and Ullman's model in which a city grows around several separate nuclei rather than a single centre.
note: Proposed jointly with Edward Ullman.

name: Conurbation
summary: Geddes's term for a large urban region formed when growing towns merge into one continuous built-up area.
note: Coined in Cities in Evolution (1915).

name: Megalopolis
summary: Gottmann's term for a chain of merged metropolitan areas, first applied to the Boston-Washington seaboard.
note: Set out in his book Megalopolis (1961).

name: Whittlesey's agricultural regions
aliases: Major Agricultural Regions of the Earth
summary: Whittlesey's division of the world into thirteen major agricultural regions using five criteria such as crop and livestock association and intensity.

name: Cycle of erosion
aliases: geographical cycle|Davisian cycle|normal cycle of erosion|geomorphic cycle|peneplain
summary: Davis's model in which uplifted land is worn down through youth, maturity and old age to a peneplain, as a function of structure, process and stage.

name: Penck's model of landform development
aliases: Penck's model|slope replacement|waxing and waning development
summary: Penck's model in which landforms depend on the ratio of uplift to denudation, with slopes developing by replacement from below.

name: Pediplanation
summary: King's model in which scarps retreat parallel to themselves, leaving pediments that merge into a pediplain.

name: Uniformitarianism
aliases: present is the key to the past
summary: The principle that the processes acting on the earth today also acted in the past.
note: The phrase "the present is the key to the past" is often credited to Hutton but was coined later by Archibald Geikie.

name: Continental drift
summary: Wegener's theory that the continents were once joined as Pangaea and have since drifted apart.
note: First presented in 1912; set out in his book of 1915.

name: Sea-floor spreading
summary: Hess's idea that new oceanic crust forms at mid-ocean ridges and moves outward to be consumed at ocean trenches.
note: His paper History of Ocean Basins was published in 1962; Robert Dietz coined the term in 1961.

name: Convection current theory
summary: Holmes's theory that convection currents in the mantle, driven by radioactive heat, move the continents.
note: Proposed in the late 1920s.

name: Plate tectonics
aliases: plate tectonic theory|theory of plate tectonics
summary: The theory that the lithosphere is divided into rigid plates that move over the asthenosphere and interact at divergent, convergent and transform boundaries.
note: Credited to McKenzie and Parker (1967) and to Morgan and Le Pichon (1968).

name: Isostasy
summary: The state of balance in which crustal blocks stand on denser material below, higher land being compensated at depth.

name: Airy's concept of isostasy
summary: G.B. Airy's view that crustal blocks of the same density sink to different depths, so mountains have deep roots.

name: Pratt's concept of isostasy
summary: J.H. Pratt's view that crustal blocks reach a common level of compensation, higher blocks being of lower density.

name: Köppen's climatic classification
summary: An empirical classification into five main groups, A to E, using temperature and precipitation values linked to natural vegetation.
note: First published in 1900 and revised several times, notably in 1918 and 1936.

name: Thornthwaite's climatic classification
summary: Classifications of climate by precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, and later by potential evapotranspiration.
note: Two schemes: 1931 and 1948.

name: Hadley cell
summary: The thermally direct circulation in which air rises near the equator and sinks near 30 degrees latitude, feeding the trade winds.
note: Named after George Hadley's 1735 explanation of the trade winds.

name: El Niño-Southern Oscillation
summary: The coupled ocean-atmosphere cycle in which El Niño warming of the eastern Pacific goes with a see-saw of pressure across the Pacific.
note: Gilbert Walker identified and named the Southern Oscillation.

name: Bergeron-Findeisen process
summary: Raindrops form when ice crystals in a cloud grow at the expense of supercooled water droplets, then fall and melt.

name: Thermal theory of the monsoon
aliases: Halley's theory of monsoon|thermal concept of monsoon
summary: Edmond Halley's explanation of the monsoon as a giant land and sea breeze caused by the unequal heating of land and sea.

name: Subsidence theory of coral reefs
summary: Darwin's theory that fringing reefs become barrier reefs and then atolls as their volcanic island slowly subsides.
note: Set out in The Structure and Distribution of Coral Reefs (1842).

name: Ecosystem
summary: Tansley's term for a community of organisms together with its physical environment, functioning as one unit.

name: Damodar Valley Corporation
summary: India's first multipurpose river valley project, set up by an Act of Parliament on the model of the Tennessee Valley Authority.

name: Planning Commission
summary: Set up by a resolution of the Government of India to draw up five-year plans, with the Prime Minister as chairman.
note: Khullar: constituted in 1950; another Khullar passage says set up by a Resolution in March 1951.

name: First Five Year Plan
summary: India's first five-year plan, which gave priority to agriculture, irrigation and power.

name: National Development Council
summary: Body of the Prime Minister, Union ministers and state chief ministers set up to approve five-year plans and bring the states into planning.

name: Community Development Programme
summary: Launched on Gandhi Jayanti to develop rural areas block by block through people's participation.

name: States Reorganisation Commission
summary: Commission under Fazl Ali, set up in 1953, whose 1955 report led to the reorganisation of states largely on linguistic lines.

name: States Reorganisation Act
summary: Act that reorganised India into 14 states and 6 union territories, largely on linguistic lines.
note: Came into force on 1 November 1956.

name: Indus Waters Treaty
summary: Treaty brokered by the World Bank that gave India the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) and Pakistan the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).

name: High Yielding Varieties Programme
summary: Programme that spread high-yielding seeds with fertiliser and irrigation and began the Green Revolution.
note: Launched in 1966-67.

name: Drought Prone Areas Programme
summary: Area development programme to reduce the effects of drought through watershed development, soil conservation and afforestation.
note: Launched in 1973-74.

name: Command Area Development Programme
summary: Programme to close the gap between irrigation potential created and used in the command areas of major and medium projects.
note: Launched in 1974-75.

name: Tribal Sub-Plan
summary: Strategy of earmarking plan funds for areas of tribal concentration, introduced in the Fifth Five Year Plan.
note: Introduced in 1974-75.

name: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
summary: Regional association of South Asian countries founded at Dhaka with seven members; Afghanistan joined in 2007.

name: 73rd Constitutional Amendment
summary: Gave constitutional status to panchayats and made them units of local planning, the basis of decentralised planning.
note: Passed in 1992; came into force on 24 April 1993.

name: 74th Constitutional Amendment
summary: Gave constitutional status to urban local bodies and provided for district and metropolitan planning committees.
note: Passed in 1992; came into force on 1 June 1993.

name: First Census of India
summary: The first population census of India, conducted at different times in different parts of the country.
note: Not synchronous; the first synchronous census was held in 1881.

name: Great Divide of 1921
aliases: Year of the Great Divide|1921 great divide
summary: The census year after which India's population has grown in every decade; 1911-21 is the only decade with a fall.

name: National Population Policy 2000
summary: Set goals of meeting contraceptive needs, reaching replacement-level fertility by 2010 and a stable population by 2045.

name: Bhuj earthquake
summary: Earthquake centred near Bhuj in Kachchh, Gujarat, on Republic Day, one of the deadliest in India.

name: Indian Ocean tsunami
summary: An earthquake off Sumatra set off a tsunami that struck the coasts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

name: Disaster Management Act
summary: Set up the National Disaster Management Authority under the Prime Minister, with state and district authorities.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
summary: Mission for urban infrastructure, basic services to the urban poor and governance reforms in selected cities.

name: NITI Aayog
summary: Policy think tank of the Government of India that replaced the Planning Commission and works through cooperative federalism.
